notices.description:
The Office of the District Attorney of New York county (DANY) seeks proposals from qualified organizations to continue and expand its Neighborhood Navigator Initiative which has had a positive impact on the Manhattan Neighborhoods currently served. DANY seeks a single organization to: (1) deliver client and community engagement and coordination teams across five designated Manhattan neighborhoods and (2) respond to areas in Manhattan outside of the five designated neighborhoods in response to emerging or immediate areas of concern as requested by DANY, which may include coordinated outreach in the outdoor spaces around select New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) developments.

DANY will hold a Pre-proposal Conference via Microsoft Teams on October 29, 2026 at 12:00pm. Attendance by proposers is optional but recommended by the Department.

Questions about this RFP may be submitted in writing to bidsrfps@dany.nyc.gov with a copy to velozm@dany.nyc.gov no later than October 21st, 2026. Questions submitted after the Q&A due date will not receive a response. Answers to questions received will be made available as an addendum to this RFP.

notices.description:
In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Probation (DOP) is requesting approval to extend the existing contract with Good Shepherd Services, (GSS) through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) to support the continuation of services under the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) Program. The contract term is from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028 in the amount of 2,145,203.52 for this period. 

The AIM Program is an Alternative to Placement (ATP) intervention designed for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation. The program provides intensive, community-based mentoring through a one-on-one model that pairs participants with paid advocate-mentors who are available around the clock and serve as consistent, trusted supports. Advocate-mentors are credible messengers with strong ties to the communities served and lived experience that enables effective engagement with participants. Over an approximately six- to nine-month, court-mandated period, youth receive individualized support focused on improving decision-making, strengthening family and community connections, and reducing further justice system involveme…

The New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission is seeking to retain one vendor to provide a Technical Project Manager for our Finance & Administration Offices. TLC anticipates awarding one contract to a city-certified Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprise (M/WBE).

The Teachers Retirement System of the City of New York (TRS) is seeking a qualified consultant to develop a practical strategic plan for the next three to five years. The consultant will work with TRS leadership and key stakeholders to assess organizational needs, establish priorities, and define measurable goals to improve member service and operational effectiveness.

notices.vendor_name: Fund for the City of New York, Inc
notices.description:
COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs.

notices.description:
Immigrant Family Services: Bronx

DYCD plans to extend their Immigrant Families contracts. These providers deliver comprehensive services for immigrant families living in low income neighborhoods throughout the city of New York. The goal of the comprehensive services to immigrant families is to:  Identify the complex and multiple needs of newly-arrived limited English proficiency families, and, in collaboration with a network of community-based providers, ensure that they gain access to services that help them become self-sufficient and prosper. Help each enrolled family build the self-advocacy skills and gain the knowledge to enable them to address specific challenges and navigate key systems that impact their lives (for example, the education, healthcare, housing, benefits, tax, workplace, and legal and immigration systems).
